title: targetdir.bats:720 says it needs no cargo, and fails on a machine with cargo off PATH
body:
FOUND 2026-10-14 by devbin's full suite on kovacs (Ubuntu 26.04.1 on aarch64, uutils coreutils 0.10.0, mawk, bats 1.12.0, shellcheck 0.11.0, GNU parallel at 2 jobs), ORDER D1 at main 2ff34a98, whose lib/ and tests/ are main's at filing (89cae16e, 2026-10-15; every line cited below re-read there): 2306 of 2307 ok and 1 not ok, seal 20261014-1024 on kovacs, 10:24:24Z to 10:49:25Z. cargo is installed there but was not on PATH for the run: rustup puts it in ~/.cargo/bin, which only an interactive shell adds. Read by vc in the seal and in the code; not driven on the Mac.

WHAT HAPPENS:
- tests/unit/targetdir.bats:720, "a machine config beside a config above TMPDIR, with no crate here, is reported as not measured, never as moving nothing (0164)", asserts at :733 the verdict for a probe a config above TMPDIR clouds: "machine <home>/config.toml names target-dir or include, and where it alone sends a build could not be measured: a cargo config at or above <proj>/.tmp may apply too -- not failed". Its comment at :723 says "It gives up before cargo is asked, so this needs no cargo", and it carries no need_cargo.
- cargo_probe_build_dir (lib/helpers:1617, reached through cargo_home_build_dir at :1667) checks `command -v cargo` before anything else (:1625). With no cargo it warns "cargo is not on PATH, so where the machine's cargo config sends a build cannot be measured" and returns 1, by design: its comment says the absence is said once, plainly. The test for a config above the probe's scratch directory, which returns 2, comes after it (:1650). So with cargo off PATH, check targetdir (lib/cmd/check:1010-1019) prints the status-1 line, "machine <home>/config.toml names target-dir or include, and where it sends a build could not be measured (the error above says why) -- not failed", and the arm fails at :733.
- The probe does give up before cargo is RUN. It is not true that it needs no cargo. Both verdicts are honest, not measured and not failed, so check targetdir is not wrong: the arm's claim is.
- Every other arm of the 2307 passed or skipped on that run with cargo off PATH, 63 of them skipped through need_cargo, so this arm is the only one with this dependence.
- CI's runners and hv's Mac both have cargo on PATH, so neither can see it. Any machine that runs devbin's suite without cargo on PATH fails it, kovacs among them.

WHAT A FIX MUST DO (cc builds it and vc reviews it):
- The arm passes on a machine with no cargo on PATH, and still checks the clouded verdict wherever it can. Either it puts a stub cargo on PATH that fails loudly if it is run, so the arm runs everywhere and its claim that cargo is never asked becomes an assertion, or it takes need_cargo, as the arms at :737 and :754 do, and skips saying so. The builder chooses and says why.
- The comment at :723 says what is true.
- check targetdir's order stays as it is, unless the builder finds a reason to change it and says what it is.
- Red first on main: the arm, run with cargo off PATH, fails at :733 as it did on kovacs. Green under BSD and GNU, with cargo on PATH and without it.

It ships in the next release, with everything open.

## Resolution

Landed at 10ae01c9 on a green full suite (vc's, 2329 of 2329 ok, 0 not ok, 5 skipped, .errors empty, seal 20261016-0917; a first run, 20261016-0858, failed only fullcycle.bats:1020 (0096), a wall-clock bound under load that this change does not touch, filed on its own).

- **The arm passes on a machine with no cargo on PATH, and still checks the clouded verdict everywhere.** It puts a stub cargo first on PATH that fails loudly if run, so it runs wherever the suite runs and asserts that the probe looks for cargo and never runs it. need_cargo would have skipped it on exactly the machines that found the defect.
- **The comment says what is true**: the probe looks for cargo on PATH first, then gives up at the config above TMPDIR before cargo would run.
- **check targetdir's order is unchanged.** Saying that cargo is not on PATH first is right for every other machine config.
- **Red first on main**, the arm with cargo off PATH, at :733 under BSD and GNU, as on kovacs. **Green** under BSD and GNU, with cargo on PATH and without it.
